course.title: AI-Powered HR
course.description: A practical, interactive introduction to AI-assisted recruitment, talent intelligence, and automated onboarding workflows.
course.audience: HR professionals, recruiters, talent acquisition specialists, and people managers
learningObjectives: Explain where generative and agentic AI realistically supports HR workflows
Apply structured screening, sourcing, and evaluation rubrics
Evaluate AI recommendations with human judgment and governance standards
Master the modern AI Recruiter's Toolkit for day-to-day operations

modules.title: Introduction to AI in Enterprise People Operations
modules.description: Foundational concepts, generative models, and responsible adoption.

lessons.title: What is AI in People Operations?
lessons.description: Core concepts and the transition from manual HR tasks to intelligent workflows.
objectives: Define artificial intelligence in practical HR terms
lessons.targetAudience: HR Professionals, People Managers, Talent Acquisition

content.text: Artificial Intelligence in enterprise HR is not about replacing human connections—it is about removing administrative friction so HR leaders can focus on culture, candidate experience, and strategic alignment.

content.title: KEY LEARNING
content.text: AI augments people; it does not remove human accountability or ethical decision-making.

questions.text: What is AI's primary and appropriate role in enterprise human resources?
options: Support repetitive manual activities while humans retain judgment
questions.feedback: AI should support speed and scale while human recruiters remain responsible for judgment, context, and decisions.

questions.text: Which principle is essential when integrating AI into people operations?
options: Maintaining human judgment, transparency, and accountability
questions.feedback: Human judgment, transparency, and accountability must always be preserved.

modules.title: The Future of Talent - AI-Driven Recruitment & Onboarding
modules.description: Deploying generative tools, semantic sourcing, automated rubrics, and personalized onboarding pipelines.

lessons.title: Module Overview & Learning Objectives
lessons.description: Strategic orientation for AI-assisted talent acquisition.
objectives: Map out the 6 primary AI talent acquisition use cases
lessons.targetAudience: Recruiters, HR Business Partners, Talent Leaders

content.text: In this module, you will discover how AI-augmented workflows empower recruiting teams to process high volumes of applicants without sacrificing quality or candidate rapport.

lessons.title: From Traditional Recruitment to AI-Augmented Recruitment
lessons.description: Comparing legacy manual screening against structured AI-assisted pipelines.
objectives: Contrast traditional sequential recruiting steps with agentic workflows
Apply productivity techniques for high-volume candidate funnels
lessons.targetAudience: Talent Acquisition Specialists, Recruiters, People Managers

content.text: From Traditional Recruitment to AI-Augmented Recruitment
Traditional recruitment often involves repetitive manual activities that consume the majority of a recruiter's daily schedule:
Generative AI can assist with many of these activities.

cards.title: Traditional Model
cards.content: Recruiter → Search → Screen → Communicate → Interview → Report

cards.title: AI-Augmented Model - IMAGE
cards.content: Recruiter + AI → Search → Prioritize → Personalize → Evaluate → Decide

content.text: The important distinction is that AI can support speed and scale, while the recruiter remains responsible for judgment, context, and decision-making.

content.title: KEY LEARNING
content.text: AI does not eliminate the recruiter. It eliminates unnecessary recruiter effort.

lessons.title: The AI Recruiter's Toolkit
lessons.description: Essential tool categories, prompt structures, and capability matrix.
objectives: Categorize AI tools across the recruitment lifecycle
Map activities to validated automation assistants
lessons.targetAudience: HR Professionals, Talent Acquisition Professionals, Recruiters, HR Business Partners, and People Managers

content.text: A practical AI Recruiter's Toolkit can include several categories of tools.

content.caption: Toolkit Mapping Matrix
rows: Generate, improve, and standardize JDs with gender-neutral phrasing
Search across talent pools and extract candidate skill profiles
Match candidate qualifications against structured role rubrics
Draft personalized invitation notes and status communications
Synthesize panel feedback and highlight skill proficiencies
Generate customized day-one schedules and team briefing packs

content.title: KEY LEARNING
content.text: Always maintain an audit trail for AI tool recommendations to ensure objective and defensible hiring processes.

questions.text: When using AI for job description creation, what is the most valuable augmentation benefit?
options: Eliminating the need to hire department managers
Standardizing requirements and auditing for inclusive language
Automatically rejecting all applicants under 5 years experience
questions.feedback: Standardizing requirements and removing subtle gendered or biased language is a major proven benefit of AI JD generators.

questions.text: Who remains accountable for candidate selection decisions in an AI-augmented workflow?
options: The software vendor who licensed the AI model
The human recruiter and hiring committee
questions.feedback: Human recruiters and hiring managers remain solely accountable for all candidate selection decisions.
